steps.reason: Large pores allow water to drain away quickly
steps.result: Soil holds little water

steps.operation: Add compost: humus binds particles into crumbs
steps.reason: Humus improves structure and holds water and nutrients
steps.result: Water retention improves

steps.operation: Add clay: smaller particles fill large pores
steps.reason: Smaller pore spaces reduce drainage and hold water
steps.result: Soil becomes loamier with better balance

content.question: Which soil would you choose for cassava, and how would capillarity help its roots in a dry week?
hints: Think of loamy soil balance
Capillarity draws water upward
Roots need air and water

lessons.title: Soil Fertility and Conservation
lessons.objective: Explain soil fertility, how it is lost, and how farmers can renew and conserve it using Nigerian practices.

content.heading: Soil Fertility and Conservation
paragraphs: Adaeze farms yam near Ibadan, but her tubers have shrunk over seasons. Her father keeps planting the same crop on the same plot without rest. She asks why the once-healthy soil no longer feeds plants well.

content.heading: What Soil Fertility Means and How It Is Lost
paragraphs: Soil fertility is the soil's ability to support plant growth by supplying water, air, and nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Fertile soil holds moisture, allows root growth, and provides humus for steady crop development.

Heavy rain leaches nutrients downward beyond roots, while erosion removes fertile top soil from bare farms. Burning, trampling and machinery compact soil, reduce air spaces, and destroy humus that improves structure and moisture.

Planting the same crop repeatedly removes similar nutrients from the same layer. Cassava and yam deplete potassium quickly, so yields fall without rest, fallow, or added organic matter to replace what harvest removed.
bullets: Leaching: rain carries dissolved nutrients below the root zone.
Erosion removes humus-rich top soil on slopes.
Compaction by feet and tractors blocks water and roots.
content.takeaway: Fertility means nutrients, humus and structure; leaching, erosion, compaction and repeated cropping destroy it.

check.question: Which practice most directly depletes the same nutrients from the same soil layer?
check.why: Repeated cropping removes similar nutrients from the same depth without replacement.

content.heading: Renewing Soil Fertility for Better Harvests
paragraphs: Crop rotation plants different crops in sequence on the same land. Legumes like cowpea and groundnut fix nitrogen through root nodules, while deep-rooted plants bring up nutrients. Rotation breaks pests and balances nutrient use across seasons.

Manure, compost and green manure add humus, improve structure, and feed soil organisms. Inorganic fertiliser such as NPK supplies nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium quickly when crops need them. Farmers in the North often combine manure with NPK for lasting improvement.

Where soil is acidic, liming with crushed limestone neutralises acidity and improves nutrient uptake. Balanced liming also benefits legumes and soil microbes, helping rice, maize and vegetable farms produce better harvests.
bullets: Rotation: alternate yam with cowpea to restore nitrogen.
Intercrop maize with groundnut between rows.
Apply compost before planting rainy-season crops.
content.takeaway: Rotation, legumes, manure, compost, NPK and lime restore nutrients and humus for fertile soil.

check.question: Which crop helps fix atmospheric nitrogen in rotation?
check.why: Cowpea is a legume whose root nodules fix nitrogen for soil and next crops.

content.heading: Conserving Soil to Prevent Further Loss
paragraphs: Mulching covers soil with grasses, crop residues, or leaves to reduce raindrop impact, evaporation, and erosion. Cover crops like melon or Mucuna keep soil protected between planting seasons, bind particles, and add organic matter when they die.

On slopes in Jos and eastern hills, contour ridging follows the land's level to trap runoff. Terracing builds step-like platforms that slow water, while strip-cropping alternates crop rows with grass strips to hold soil and cut erosion.

Mixed cropping or poly-cropping grows yam, cassava, plantain and cocoyam together, giving full cover and varied roots. In shifting cultivation, farmers clear, farm briefly, then allow fallow to regrow, restoring fertility before reuse.
bullets: Mulch with dried grasses around tomato beds.
Ridge along contours, never up and down slopes.
Mix cassava, yam and vegetables in one plot.
content.takeaway: Cover soil, slow runoff, and rest land with fallow to conserve fertility.

check.question: Which conservation method slows runoff on a hillside farm?
check.why: Contour ridging follows the level of the slope and traps runoff and eroded soil.

content.title: Exam tip
content.body: Examiners often ask for two causes of soil loss and two renewal methods. List leaching, erosion, compaction plus rotation, legumes, manures and liming, linking each choice to a Nigerian farm example for full marks.

content.problem: Mrs Bello in Kano plants maize yearly on the same sandy plot, applying little manure. Yields fall and rain washes soil. Propose a restoration plan.

steps.operation: Rotate maize with cowpea, then sorghum on different rows
steps.reason: Cowpea fixes nitrogen and crops use different nutrients
steps.result: Nutrient balance improves and pest cycles break

steps.operation: Add compost and recommended NPK; lime if test shows acidity
steps.reason: Humus restores structure and NPK replaces nutrients
steps.result: Soil holds water and feeds roots better

steps.operation: Mulch residues and ridge along contours
steps.reason: Mulch cuts evaporation and ridges slow runoff
steps.result: Top soil stays and yields stabilise

content.question: How would you help a farmer who plants only yam on one plot each year restore the soil?
hints: Think of legumes and rotation.
Which organic matter adds humus?
What covers soil to stop erosion?

lessons.title: Diseases, Vectors and Control
lessons.objective: Identify common diseases, their vectors and causes, and how communities control them.

content.heading: Diseases, Vectors and Control
paragraphs: During the dusty harmattan in Kano, Chidi gets fever and stiff neck, diagnosed as meningitis. His cousin in the Niger Delta suffers repeated malaria. How are these Nigerian diseases spread, and how are they controlled?

content.heading: Common Endemic Diseases and Their Causes
paragraphs: Malaria, Nigeria's commonest disease, is caused by Plasmodium parasites carried by female Anopheles mosquitoes. Bites during the rainy season transmit the parasites, causing fever, chills, and anaemia, especially in children under five.

Meningitis is caused by Neisseria bacteria in the throat, spreading by coughs and close contact in dry, dusty weather. Tuberculosis, or TB, is airborne: Mycobacterium germs spread through coughs and stay in crowded homes, causing persistent cough and weakness.

Cholera and typhoid spread through contaminated water and food carrying Vibrio and Salmonella bacteria. Open defecation, poor sewage, and dirty hands in markets or IDP camps allow rapid spread, causing watery diarrhoea, vomiting, and fever.
bullets: Malaria: Anopheles mosquito carries Plasmodium parasites.
Meningitis: Neisseria bacteria spread in dry season.
Cholera: Vibrio spreads via dirty water and food.
content.takeaway: Malaria, meningitis, cholera, typhoid and TB remain endemic through vectors, dust, water and air.

check.question: Which mosquito spreads Plasmodium parasites that cause malaria?
check.why: Only female Anopheles mosquitoes carry Plasmodium parasites into human blood by bites.

content.heading: Water, Insect and Contact-Borne Diseases
paragraphs: Schistosomiasis, or bilharzia, occurs when skin touches freshwater containing cercariae larvae. Freshwater snails release cercariae used for swimming, fishing, and washing in rivers, causing blood in urine and liver damage.

Onchocerciasis, or river blindness, spreads by Simulium blackflies breeding near fast streams, causing severe itching and blindness. Drancunculiasis is caused by Guinea worms spread when people drink water with copepods, leading to painful skin blisters.

Polio virus spreads through contaminated water and food, attacking nerves and causing paralysis in children. Sexually transmitted infections, including HIV, spread through unsafe sex and blood; repeated reinfection worsens illness and treatment failure.
bullets: Bilharzia: freshwater snail releases cercariae into water.
River blindness: Simulium blackfly bites near rivers.
Guinea worm: copepod in drinking water spreads disease.
content.takeaway: Snails, blackflies, copepods, contaminated water and unsafe sex transmit these diseases.

check.question: Which vector spreads onchocerciasis near fast-flowing rivers?
check.why: Simulium blackflies breed near fast streams and transmit onchocerciasis when biting.

content.heading: Controlling Diseases Across Communities
paragraphs: Bed nets, indoor spraying with insecticide, and larviciding that kills mosquito larvae reduce malaria. Clearing stagnant water, covering water jars, and improving drainage around homes also stop mosquitoes and blackflies breeding.

Boiling, chlorination, and filtering make water safe against cholera, typhoid, and polio. Pit latrines, proper sewage disposal, hand washing, and food hygiene break the faecal-oral chain in villages and camps.

Vaccination protects: Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) against polio, BCG against TB, and meningococcal vaccine against meningitis. TB patients complete DOTS therapy. WHO coordinates global policy while UNICEF supplies vaccines and water programmes.
bullets: Use insecticide-treated nets every night.
Boil or chlorinate water from wells.
Vaccinate with OPV and BCG early.
content.takeaway: Nets, clean water, sanitation, vaccines, DOTS and support agencies prevent spread.

check.question: Which agency supplies vaccines for polio immunisation in Nigeria?
check.why: UNICEF supplies vaccines, cold chains and immunisation support, while WHO sets policy.

content.title: Exam tip
content.body: Remember each disease with its pathogen, vector and control. For malaria, match Anopheles and Plasmodium to nets and spraying; for bilharzia, match snails and cercariae to clean water and avoidance of contact.

content.problem: After flooding in Benue, many families drink well water and mosquitoes breed in pools. Diarrhoea and malaria rise. What control actions should health workers take?

steps.operation: Chlorinate wells and distribute treated nets and insecticide spray
steps.reason: Chlorine kills Vibrio and Salmonella; nets and spray block Anopheles bites
steps.result: Waterborne diseases and malaria transmission fall

steps.operation: Build pit latrines away from wells and clear stagnant water
steps.reason: Sanitation stops faecal-oral spread and larviciding removes breeding sites
steps.result: Cholera risk drops and mosquito numbers fall

steps.operation: Vaccinate children with OPV and BCG; support DOTS for TB cases
steps.reason: Vaccines prevent polio and severe TB; DOTS ensures TB cure
steps.result: Outbreaks prevented and treatment completed

content.question: If bilharzia is common in a fishing village, what vector and control methods would you suggest?
hints: Think of snail and water contact.
How should drinking water be made safe?
Which nets or sprays also help?

lessons.title: Drug Abuse
lessons.objective: Define drug abuse and addiction, describe their effects, and explain ways to prevent and treat abuse.

content.heading: Drug Abuse
paragraphs: Tunde, a market trader's son in Onitsha, steals money to buy codeine syrup. He was once bright in school but now sleeps in class. How can a single habit harm his body, mind, and future?

content.heading: What Drug Abuse Means and Common Drugs
paragraphs: A drug is any substance that changes body or mind function. Drug misuse is taking it wrongly, while abuse is deliberate heavy use. Addiction means compulsive use despite harm, with tolerance and dependence developing over time.

Tolerance is needing more of the drug for the same effect, while dependence is the body craving it continuously. Withdrawal signs like shaking, sweating, and anxiety appear when use stops. Without help, users cannot easily quit despite harm.

Commonly abused in Nigeria are alcohol, cannabis (weed), codeine cough syrup, and tramadol tablets. Shisha, cocaine, and heroin are also abused, especially where peer pressure, stress, and idle youths encourage use for pleasure or escape.
bullets: Alcohol: cheap local gin harms liver quickly.
Codeine and tramadol affect brain and control.
Cannabis and shisha damage lungs and focus.
content.takeaway: Abuse means heavy, harmful use leading to tolerance, dependence and addiction.

check.question: Needing more tramadol for the same effect shows what?
check.why: Tolerance is the need for a larger dose to achieve the previous effect.

content.heading: Effects of Drug Abuse on Health and Society
paragraphs: Alcohol damages the liver, causes heart failure, and shrinks the brain. Tramadol and cocaine strain the heart, while smoking shisha and cannabis harms lungs. Overdose can cause seizures, coma, and sudden death.

Drug abuse leads to mental illness, depression, aggression, and violence at home. Users fail school, lose friends, suffer accidents while driving or operating machines, and spread infections through unsafe injections and risky sex.

Families waste school fees and trading money on drugs, deepening poverty. Stolen goods, damaged markets, and hospital costs burden communities. Government loses workers through illness, accidents, and early deaths.
bullets: Physical: liver, brain, heart, lungs weaken.
Mental: violence, depression and school failure rise.
Economic: money lost to drugs and treatment.
content.takeaway: Drugs harm body, mind and society while draining family and national wealth.

check.question: Which is a mental or social effect of drug abuse?
check.why: Violence, depression and school failure are common mental and social effects of abuse.

content.heading: Preventing and Treating Drug Abuse
paragraphs: Parents, schools and communities must teach risks early, set rules, and watch peers and friendships. Sports, music, and clubs give youths positive outlets. Counselling can rethink triggers, stress, and pressure before use becomes addiction.

Addicts need medical treatment, rehabilitation centres, spiritual support, and family backing to recover. Law enforcement arrests dealers but must not only punish users. Linking offenders to treatment saves lives and reduces crime.

NAFDAC regulates drugs and checks fake products, while NDLEA fights trafficking and abuse. In Onitsha, Tunde's mother sought counselling and rehabilitation; he supports his family after learning a trade and avoiding old friends.
bullets: Friends and family: talk early, monitor use.
Schools: sports, clubs and drug education.
NDLEA and NAFDAC check supply and sales.
content.takeaway: Education, sports, counselling, treatment and regulation together prevent and cure abuse.

check.question: Which agency fights drug trafficking in Nigeria?
check.why: NDLEA enforces drug laws and fights trafficking, while NAFDAC regulates drug quality.

content.title: Exam tip
content.body: In essays, separate definitions, effects and prevention clearly. Explain tolerance before listing alcohol, cannabis, codeine, tramadol, shisha, cocaine and heroin, then name NAFDAC and NDLEA for prevention marks.

content.problem: The market trader's son in Onitsha steals to buy codeine and fails school. His mother seeks help. Outline steps to rescue him and protect others.

steps.operation: Counselling at school and clinic to map pressure and cravings
steps.reason: Identifies triggers and builds coping strategies
steps.result: Motivation to stop and relapse plan

steps.operation: Medical treatment and rehabilitation plus family supervision
steps.reason: Treats withdrawal and restores health gradually
steps.result: Tunde withdraws safely and rebuilds routine

steps.operation: Join sports club, learn a trade, avoid drug-using friends
steps.reason: Positive outlets replace drug rewards and peer influence
steps.result: School and business recovery sustained

content.question: What steps would you take if a friend begins abusing tramadol?
hints: Tell a trusted adult early.
Think of counselling and treatment.
Which agencies fight drug abuse?

lessons.title: Pollution, Conservation and National Parks
lessons.objective: Describe pollution types and control, and explain conservation of resources and national parks in Nigeria.

content.heading: Pollution, Conservation and National Parks
paragraphs: Kola farms near Lagos Lagoon and sees empty nets as oil and plastic clog his water. Smoke darkens the mornings. He asks how pollution harms people and how nature can be protected.

content.heading: Types of Pollution and Their Effects
paragraphs: Air pollution comes from smoke, carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2), vehicle exhaust, and generator fumes common in cities. It causes asthma, coughing, and heart problems, while reducing visibility and acidifying rain.

Water pollution comes from sewage, industrial effluent, and oil spills in rivers and lagoons. It kills fish, spreads cholera, and makes water unsafe. Oil films also smother birds and damage mangrove roots.

Land pollution comes from plastics, e-waste, market waste, and dumped chemicals. It blocks drains, breeds mosquitoes, harbours rats, and poisons soils. Children playing near dumps risk infections and heavy-metal exposure.
bullets: Air: smoke, CO, SO2, exhaust, generators.
Water: sewage, effluent, oil spills kill fish.
Land: plastics, e-waste, market waste poison soil.
content.takeaway: Pollution harms health and ecosystems through air, water and land wastes.

check.question: Which gases cause air pollution near generators and vehicles?
check.why: Generators and vehicles release CO and SO2, harming lungs and vegetation.

content.heading: Controlling Pollution in Towns and Industries
paragraphs: Proper sanitation, pit latrines, and sewage treatment stop water contamination. Regulation forces factories to treat effluent before discharge. Clean markets, drains, and water stores prevent cholera and mosquito breeding.

Segregating solid waste into plastics, paper, organics, and e-waste aids composting and recycling. Market sweepings can become compost, while collection crews must clear dumps promptly. Personal hygiene, including hand washing, closes disease routes.

Traps, scrubbers, and filters on chimneys reduce smoke and sulphur gases. Cleaner fuels, vehicle exhaust checks, and tree planting also cut air pollution. Laws and fines, enforced by environmental officers, keep polluters accountable.
bullets: Treat sewage and factory effluent before release.
Segregate waste for composting and recycling.
Use scrubbers, filters and cleaner fuels.
content.takeaway: Treat wastes, segregate solids, trap emissions and enforce hygiene laws.

check.question: Which method recycles market organic waste into useful material?
check.why: Composting turns organic market waste into valuable fertiliser for soils.

content.heading: Conservation, Parks and Protecting Nature
paragraphs: Renewable resources like forests, fisheries, and soils can regrow if managed well. Non-renewable resources such as minerals and fossil fuels, including coal and oil, have fixed amounts and cannot easily replace once used.

Conservation protects biodiversity, prevents erosion and desertification, and secures clean water and timber. In the North, shelterbelts, agroforestry, and anti-desertification belts stop wind and shifting sands threatening farms and homes.

The Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), Federal Ministry of Environment, and National Parks Service manage reserves. Internationally, WWF, IUCN, and UNEP support conservation. Parks include Cross River, Gashaka-Gumti, Yankari, Chad Basin, Kainji Lake, and Old Oyo; Borgu is a game reserve.
bullets: Renewable: forests, fisheries, soils regrow.
Non-renewable: minerals, oil, coal exhaust.
Parks: Yankari, Cross River, Old Oyo, Borgu.
content.takeaway: Protect renewables, use non-renewables wisely, and guard parks for future generations.

check.question: Which is a national park in south-eastern Nigeria?
check.why: Cross River National Park is in the south-east, while others are in other zones.

content.title: Exam tip
content.body: Learn parks with states and products: name Cross River, Gashaka-Gumti, Yankari, Chad Basin, Kainji Lake and Old Oyo. Distinguish renewable forests and fisheries from non-renewable oil and minerals in short definitions.

content.problem: Dust and smoke from a Lagos market dump and factory effluent pollute air and water. Propose pollution control and conservation actions.

steps.operation: Segregate market waste; compost organics and recycle plastics and e-waste
steps.reason: Less dumping, less drain blockage and compost enriches soil
steps.result: Dumps shrink and water contamination falls

steps.operation: Treat factory effluent and fit chimneys with scrubbers and filters
steps.reason: Traps smoke and sulphur gases before release
steps.result: Air and river cleaner

steps.operation: Plant shelterbelts and protect a nearby forest as a reserve
steps.reason: Trees cut wind, bind soil and preserve biodiversity
steps.result: Anti-desertification and habitat protected

content.question: Which resources would you conserve first in your town, and where would you learn about protected parks?
hints: Separate renewables from non-renewables.
Think of forests, soils and fisheries.
Name one Nigerian park or reserve.
